top_news.title: Houthis claim fresh wave of strikes on Saudi airports and oil facilities, call airspace
top_news.summary: Yemeni Houthi forces claimed responsibility on Sunday for launching four major operations involving ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones against Saudi airports and energy infrastructure over a 24-hour period, declaring Saudi airspace unsafe with the explicit exception of the holy cities of Mecca and Medina. The rebel group's announcement came as King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh was struck again on Sunday, its second attack within 24 hours and third this week, when a projectile hit Terminal 4 and ignited a fire, following a devastating assault a day earlier that left 12 people dead and over 300 injured. According to an official statement shared by Houthi military spokesperson Brigadier General Yahya Saree on Telegram, the group framed the cross-border strikes as direct retaliation for recent coalition bombardment, stating, "In response to the brutal Saudi aggression against our country and our people, which launched 124 airstrikes in the past 24 hours, targeting the capital Sana'a and the governorates of Taiz, Ma'rib, Al-Jawf, Hajjah, Al-Hudaydah, and Sa'dah, bringing the total number of airstrikes since the beginning of the escalation against our country up to 2,058, committing massacres against our people, the majority of whose victims are women and children." Claiming extensive operations deep inside Saudi territory, the Houthi statement outlined the deployment of advanced weaponry across key targets. "With Allah's help, the Armed Forces carried out four qualitative operations in the past 24 hours using ballistic and cruise missiles and drones," the statement read. Detailing the individual operations, the rebel group claimed responsibility for targeting Saudi Arabia's main international hubs, asserting that air traffic was crippled in both the capital and the Eastern Province. Regarding the assault on the capital's aviation facilities, the statement claimed, "The first operation targeted in three phases King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh starting the evening before last, resulting in the disruption of air traffic and the complete closure of the airport." The statement further claimed a separate strike targeting Dammam's primary airport, noting, "The fourth operation targeted King Fahd International Airport in Dammam. The strike was direct and resulted in the disruption of air traffic at the airport." In addition to aviation targets, the rebel group claimed precise strikes against state oil giant Saudi Aramco's energy infrastructure in the Eastern Province. Describing the attack on gas infrastructure, the spokesperson stated, "The second operation targeted the Shugadam gas facility belonging to Aramco in the Eastern Province, and the strike was accurate, thanks be to Allah, and resulted in large fires breaking out at the targeted site." Regarding energy processing assets, the statement added, "The third operation targeted the Aramco Tanajib oil refinery in the Eastern Province. The strike was also accurate, thanks be to Allah, and resulted an ignition in it." The movement also claimed responsibility for military strikes against troop concentrations, stating, "In another development, our armed forces carried out a precise targeting operation against Saudi enemy buildups in the Ras al-Ara and al-Saqiya areas with six ballistic missiles and two drones, and the strikes were accurate, thanks be to Allah, and resulted in killing and wounding dozens of the enemy troops." Amid the military escalation, the Houthis issued a broad warning to international airlines, foreign workers, and commercial travellers to avoid Saudi aviation hubs, declaring Saudi airspace unsafe with the explicit exception of the holy cities of Mecca and Medina. "We reiterate our warning to all international companies, experts, employees, workers, and travellers from all over the world to not operate flights to Saudi airports, as they are unsafe, except for the airports and airspace of the holy cities of Mecca and Medina," the statement read. Vowing to maintain military pressure across the border until regional operations cease, the group concluded,"The Yemeni Armed Forces will continue their escalating operations deep inside Saudi, imposing the equation of "a blockade for a blockade" and "an escalation for an escalation" and targeting Saudi enemy reinforcements until the aggression ceases and the siege on our dear people is lifted." The statement comes as King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi capital was targeted in a fresh assault on Sunday, marking the second attack on the facility within 24 hours, as air defence forces intercepted a cruise missile and emergency responders tackled a fire sparked by an incoming projectile. The latest strike comes a day after a devastating attack at the same airport left 12 people dead and over 300 injured, severely disrupting international air traffic across the region. Confirming the fresh aerial threat, the Official Spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen, Major General Turki Al-Malki, stated that Saudi air defences successfully intercepted an incoming missile in the immediate vicinity of the capital's main aviation hub, according to statements reported by the Saudi Press Agency (SPA). "Official Spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen Major General Turki Al-Malki stated that the air defence intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile in the vicinity of King Khalid International Airport," the Saudi Press Agency reported. The interception followed an earlier breach at the complex where an incoming weapon struck passenger infrastructure, igniting a blaze inside the facility. Earlier, Major General Al-Malki stated that "Terminal 4 at King Khalid International Airport was struck by an unidentified projectile, resulting in a fire," adding that "the relevant authorities are currently responding to the incident." Emergency services and first responders were deployed to contain the blaze and secure the terminal. The back-to-back strikes highlight a sharp escalation in regional aerial attacks targeting critical civilian and aviation infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. This development unfolded as Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV reported that Saudi forces had initiated a fresh barrage of air and missile strikes across territories controlled by the group in Yemen, striking Sanaa International Airport in the capital, regions near the strategic Bab al-Mandeb Strait and various northern provinces. However, the Saudi-led coalition has not yet confirmed this strike. International condemnation has intensified following an attack carried out by Houthi forces targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, which sparked widespread global concern amid ongoing regional hostilities. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has strongly condemned the deadly "terrorist" attack, extending Israel's condolences to the victims' families while calling for regional unity against shared security threats. The statement, issued by the Israeli Prime Minister's Office, denounced the strike and emphasised the necessity of a decisive response to terror across the Middle East. "I condemn in the strongest possible terms the horrific terrorist attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, which claimed the lives of 12 innocent people and injured hundreds more," Netanyahu stated. Expressing solidarity with those affected by the fatal assault, the Israeli Prime Minister extended his sympathy to the families of the victims and those recovering from their injuries, stating, "On behalf of the people of Israel, I extend our deepest condolences to the families of those murdered and our wishes for a full recovery to the injured." Framing the assault as a broader attempt to destabilise the region, Netanyahu stressed that extremist threats require resolute action from regional actors. "Terrorism targets innocent people and seeks to spread fear and instability. It must be confronted with resolve," he said. Looking ahead at regional security dynamics, Netanyahu reaffirmed Israel's vision for a collaborative security architecture across the Middle East, saying,"Israel looks forward to a strong Middle East-one that stands united against threats, protects its people, and builds a future of security, cooperation, and prosperity for all the peoples of our region." On the other hand, US President Donald Trump stated that Washington was evaluating whether to join Saudi Arabia's strikes against Yemen's Houthi rebels following the lethal assault on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport. When asked if a decision had been made to participate in the Saudi strikes, Trump stated, "We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack. We will make a decision. We move very quickly." He further added, "Look, the Saudis are good fighters. But I think the attack was a terrible thing." US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the attack a "blatant disregard for innocent civilian life" and affirmed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and its people. "The United States strongly condemns the recent attacks on the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia by the terrorist Houthis, including today's strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that took numerous innocent lives, including an American citizen. These reprehensible attacks demonstrate a blatant disregard for innocent civilian life. They must stop now. We stand with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and its people and extend our condolences to the victims and their families," Rubio wrote in a post on X. In response to the escalation, the US Mission in Saudi Arabia issued a security alert on Sunday, directing American nationals to steer clear of King Khalid International Airport and adjacent zones following the October 10 strikes. The mission also cautioned travellers to exercise extreme vigilance at major Saudi airports, warning of potential flight cancellations, airspace restrictions and travel disruptions, while advising passengers to verify flight statuses directly with operators. Furthermore, the mission announced that US government personnel stationed in Saudi Arabia need special authorisation to use King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, alongside facilities in Jeddah and Dammam. These developments are anticipated to heighten pressure on Riyadh's international partners, including the United States, to extend military backing as the Kingdom intensifies operations against the Houthis. According to figures released by the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation, the 12 victims who died in the Saturday afternoon strike comprised four Saudi nationals alongside eight foreign residents, two from Bangladesh and one each from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan. Medical personnel are treating the 309 wounded individuals across multiple hospitals, with some patients listed in serious condition. Subsequently, the Indian authorities are coordinating with the Saudi authorities regarding the 11 nationals injured, out of which one succumbed to injuries, in the "dastardly attack" targeting King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi capital of Riyadh. In a post on X, the Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia said that it has been following up with the authorities after the attack, noting that the embassy officials also reached out to the hospital authorities where the injured Indian nationals are being treated. This came after India strongly condemned the deadly strike targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, while affirming its firm solidarity with Saudi Arabia in protecting its sovereignty. New Delhi asserted that the assault on civilian areas and vital installations was entirely unjustifiable. In the statement, the Ministry of External Affairs noted, "The repeated attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are completely unacceptable and must cease immediately." Reiterating India's diplomatic position, the MEA added, "We stand in solidarity with the people and the government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty, and hope that peace and normalcy return to the region at the earliest." Additionally, Dhaka issued a stern warning that it will take all necessary measures to protect Islamic holy sites in Mecca and Medina if they come under threat, following the deadly Houthi strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that killed two Bangladeshi pilgrims and forced the temporary suspension of all flights between Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia. "Bangladesh strongly and unequivocally condemns the deadly Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on 10 October 2026, which resulted in casualties, including the tragic loss of two Bangladeshi nationals, and left numerous others injured, many of them critically. Bangladesh mission in Riyadh is in contact with the Saudi authorities to obtain details of the deceased and injured Bangladeshis and to facilitate necessary assistance to those affected," the statement from the Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs read. Weighing in on the incident, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres took to social media to express his outrage over the offensive. In a post on X, he stated, "I am deeply shocked by and strongly condemn Saturday's lethal attack by the Houthis on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, which reportedly killed 12 people and injured hundreds of civilians. Attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are a violation of international law. These attacks must cease immediately." The strike follows a string of recent attacks directed at King Khalid International Airport over the past week. The Houthis previously claimed responsibility for assaults on the facility that left three Saudis dead, including a pilot. This surge in violence has also targeted other Saudi airfields, military installations and petroleum infrastructure, following a major military offensive initiated against the Houthis by a Saudi-led coalition the previous week. (ANI)

top_news.title: Arunachal Pradesh Cabinet congratulates PM Modi on completing 25 Years as head of government
top_news.summary: The Arunachal Pradesh Cabinet, led by Chief Minister Pema Khandu, on behalf of the people of the state, on Sunday joined crores of Indians in celebrating Prime Minister Narendra Modi completing 25 years of continuous service as head of government on October 7. PM Modi took the oath as Chief Minister of Gujarat on October 7, 2001 and continued through his service as Prime Minister of India from May 26, 2014 onwards. His third consecutive term began on June 9, 2024. In a press release issued by the CMO, Arunachal Pradesh stated that the state cabinet recorded that, across PM Modi's journey, his responsibilities have grown while his devotion to Bharat Mata has remained constant. From his early work at the grassroots to leadership of a state and the nation, the spirit of Seva Hi Samarpan has consistently guided his public life. Describing himself as the Pradhan Sevak, he placed service at the centre of governance and worked with discipline, perseverance and tireless dedication under the mantra of 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas and Sabka Prayas'. "The Cabinet highlighted the national transformation achieved under his leadership, from welfare, economic strength and national security to technology, infrastructure and renewed pride in India's heritage. Decisive actions, including the abrogation of Article 370, the replacement of colonial-era laws with the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Goods and Services Tax and next-generation GST 2.0 reforms, reflect a consistent commitment to national interest. The Cabinet also expressed its collective profound gratitude to the Prime Minister for launching the next-gen GST 2.0 reforms and the GST Bachat Utsav during his visit Itanagar on 22 September 2025, the first day of the pious occasion of Navratri. It is particularly significant that this resolution of the Cabinet was passed on 11th October, the first day of Navratri this year," said in the CMO Arunachal Pradesh statement. It also stated that Arunachal Pradesh has been a proud partner in this developmental journey. The State achieved 100 per cent saturation under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana, covering more than 8.57 lakh beneficiaries. Around 55,000 families received pucca houses registered in the names of women, while 2.28 lakh houses received functional household tap connections, making Arunachal Pradesh the first State in the North East to achieve 100% saturation under the Jal Jeevan Mission. More than 2.26 lakh families are covered under AB PM-JAY and CMAAY, providing cashless treatment of up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year. "The Prime Minister's focus on Annadata, Nari Shakti and Yuva Shakti has strengthened livelihoods and opened new opportunities across the State and throughout the nation. More than 1.14 lakh farmers from Arunachal Pradesh have been enrolled under PM-KISAN, with over Rs 150 crore transferred directly to their bank accounts. Nearly one lakh women have been mobilised into 15,999 Self-Help Groups; more than 16,000 have become Lakhpati Didis, with 36,000 more identified to reach this goal. 50 government schools have been upgraded into Golden Jubilee Model Schools, 58 Khelo India Centres now reach every district, and 156 startups have been supported with seed funding of more than Rs 5.59 crore, of which 45.5% are led by women," the CMO said. The Cabinet also noted the remarkable infrastructure transformation in Arunachal Pradesh. The Sela and Nechiphu tunnels have enhanced all-weather connectivity, strengthened strategic mobility and promoted tourism. Donyi Polo Airport, the State's first greenfield airport, can handle one million passengers a year, while Tezu Airport has been upgraded with a new terminal building. Under the Vibrant Villages Programme, 455 villages across 11 districts were selected in Phase I, with 1,022 km of roads worth Rs 2,205 crore approved to connect 126 border villages. A further 122 villages along the Myanmar and Bhutan borders have been included in Phase II, making frontier communities partners in development and national security," CMO Arunachal Pradesh stated in the press statement. It further stated that Arunachal Pradesh is also emerging as a future powerhouse of India. "The 2,000 MW Subansiri Lower Hydroelectric Project has been developed at a cost of Rs 30,071 crore, with 4 units commissioned and the remaining units expected shortly. Investment of more than Rs 52,000 crore has been approved for 5 additional hydropower projects that will generate almost 4,000 MW of renewable energy and support India's net zero goals. The Cabinet further expressed gratitude for the support in recognition, preservation and promotion of Arunachal Pradesh's rich indigenous, tribal and Buddhist heritage, cultures and traditions. 20 indigenous products have secured Geographical Indication tags. The Union Budget for 2026-27 announced a scheme to develop Buddhist circuits in six Northeastern States, including Arunachal Pradesh, while rare manuscripts and medical manuscripts are being documented and digitised under the Gyan Bharatam Mission," it said. "Under the Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment, Rs 4,900 crore has been allocated to Arunachal Pradesh under the Pride of Hills component. The Cabinet collectively renewed its commitment and resolve to build upon these achievements to form a strong foundation for the national resolve of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. It extended heartfelt congratulations to Narendra Modi, expressed profound gratitude for his life of service and tireless dedication, and reaffirmed Arunachal Pradesh's resolve to work under his guidance towards a prosperous, secure, self-reliant and developed India," said in the press statement. In other decisions, the Cabinet also approved a series of decisions aimed at strengthening higher and technical education, improving healthcare services, expanding support for women in distress, and streamlining administrative and institutional frameworks across the state. Among the key decisions, the Cabinet approved uniform, merit-based recruitment rules for several teaching and technical positions in government engineering and polytechnic colleges. In a significant step towards standardising recruitment in technical education institutions, the Cabinet approved recruitment rules for 12 categories of posts in government engineering and polytechnic colleges in accordance with the applicable All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) Regulations of 2019. The approved rules cover the posts of Principal in government polytechnic colleges and government engineering colleges; Assistant Professor, Associate Professor and Professor in government engineering colleges; Workshop Superintendent, Assistant Librarian, Laboratory Assistant, Senior Technical Assistant and System Analyst in government engineering colleges; and Head of Department (Civil Engineering) in government polytechnic colleges. The rules are intended to establish a transparent, merit-based and uniform mechanism for appointments, in line with the AICTE Diploma and Degree Regulations, 2019. To strengthen support for women facing distress and emergencies, the State Cabinet approved the creation of 20 posts to operationalise the Women Helpline-181 scheme, in accordance with Mission Shakti guidelines. Women Helpline-181 is a toll-free, round-the-clock service intended to provide emergency assistance and immediate response to women in distress, while connecting them with services such as medical care, shelter, legal aid, emotional support and guidance. The State Cabinet approved the renaming of Government College, Seppa, in East Kameng district, as Donglo Sonam Government College, Wessang, in honour of Late Donglo Sonam, recognised for his contribution to the growth and development of East Kameng district and Arunachal Pradesh. The State Cabinet also approved the naming of the Government Higher Secondary School, Daporijo, as the Lt Punji Mara Government Higher Secondary School, Daporijo and the naming of the Government Model Degree College, Daporijo, as the Popak Bage Government Model Degree College, Reempu Yorlo. The State Cabinet approved enhancement of grade pay for different categories of posts under the National Leprosy Elimination Programme (NLEP) in the Department of Health and Family Welfare. The decision seeks to address concerns regarding wage parity and fairness, improve staff morale and productivity, and strengthen the delivery of patient care and rehabilitation services. In another healthcare-related decision, the Arunachal Pradesh Cabinet approved the creation of five posts of Food Safety Officer, Group B, Gazetted Non-Ministerial. The new posts are intended to address manpower gaps in the State's food-law enforcement machinery and strengthen food-safety monitoring and enforcement to protect public health. (ANI)

top_news.title: Revanth Reddy exudes confidence in Congress
top_news.summary: Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy on Sunday expressed confidence that the Congress would come to power in Goa in the 2027 Assembly elections, saying he sensed the same optimism in the state that he had experienced in Telangana ahead of the 2023 polls. He urged voters to support the Congress's 'Hand' symbol and alleged that smaller parties emerging in Goa were being propped up by the BJP to divide votes. Addressing a gathering as part of the Congress' Goy Rakhonn Yatra, Revanth Reddy appealed to the people not to vote for smaller parties, claiming that their votes would ultimately benefit the BJP. They are here to divide the people. Any vote for them is a vote for BJP. This time, I urge the people of Goa, vote only for the Hand symbol, he said. Drawing a comparison between the Congress and the BJP through the Ramayan, the Telangana Chief Minister said, Ravan is BJP, which is dividing the people, and Ram is Congress. If you want to defeat Ravan, you have to support Ram, he said. Revanth Reddy said South Goa had traditionally been a Congress stronghold but alleged that the emergence of smaller parties could help the BJP retain power if voters did not support the Congress. Emphasising the need for voters to make their choice carefully, he said, Without voting for the Hand symbol, you cannot defeat BJP. Think twice before you vote. Who do you want running this state? Drug lords? Builder mafia? If you make a mistake once, you can move on. If you make it twice, you can still correct it. If you make the same mistake thrice, not even God can save us, he said. He said that while Congress leader Rahul Gandhi was working to unite people, the BJP was attempting to divide them. Revanth Reddy also explained why he was representing Rahul Gandhi at the gathering, saying the Congress leader had been required to remain in Delhi to lead the party's fight against the Union government. But yesterday, I got a call from Shri Mallikarjun Kharge ji. He said Rahul ji is needed in Delhi, where he is leading the fight for our country. Kharge ji told me to represent Rahul ji here. Rahul ji told him that Congress party workers in Goa are waiting. I am here as a messenger and representative of Rahul ji, he said. He described Rahul Gandhi as leading the youth, the Opposition and the country in a fight against what he called the corrupt dictatorship of the Modi government. Congratulating Goa Assembly Leader of Opposition Yuri Alemao and Goa Pradesh Congress Committee president Girish Chodankar for organising the yatra, Revanth Reddy conveyed greetings from Telangana and recalled the Congress' campaign ahead of the 2023 Assembly elections in his state. As Chief Minister of Telangana, I bring love and greetings from the people of Telangana. I remember how we, too, in Telangana had done a similar padayatra. I also note that there is optimism in the air here in Goa. It is the same optimism I found in Telangana ahead of the Assembly elections in 2023, when we won and formed the government there, he said. He said people were clear that the BJP government should not be allowed to return to power for a third term in Goa and alleged that the state's land was being transferred to others. I asked someone in a temple who their CM was. They told me the CM's name was 'Property Sawant'. The people of Goa elected him to lead the state, but that's not what he is doing. He is selling and giving away the land of Goa to others, said the Chief Minister. Revanth Reddy also raised concerns over unemployment and drug use among Goa's youth, recounting a conversation he had with a young person earlier in the day. He said things are very bad; there are no jobs. Then what are they doing, I asked. He said they are handling the stress badly and the youth are indulging in drugs. Goa has become a den of drugs, he said. Comparing the situation with Hyderabad before the Congress came to power in Telangana in 2023, he said his government had established the EAGLE force, an elite team of officers tasked with eradicating drugs in the state. After we took charge, I created the EAGLE force, an elite group of officers to eradicate drugs in Telangana. I came to know that a lot of the drugs are coming from Goa. We sent a team to Goa, and we found a large network of smugglers here, he said. He challenged Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant to explain why the state government had not taken effective action against drug trafficking, despite the Centre's stated objective of making India drug-free. The whole of the Indian government is on your side. The Prime Minister and Home Minister are saying Nasha Mukt Bharat. My question is simple - why are you not implementing it in Goa? It is because you are making money off drugs, he said. Questioning the BJP government's ability to tackle the problem, he asked whether Goa's association with drugs was good for the state and why the authorities had failed to control the issue despite the Enforcement Directorate (ED), the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and other agencies being under the BJP's control. BJP has ruined Goa, he declared. The Telangana Chief Minister also accused the BJP-led Union government of undermining democracy and alleged that the Election Commission of India (ECI) was being misused to remove voters from electoral rolls through the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government is destroying democracy in India. They have destroyed the Election Commission. They are misusing SIR to remove the votes of crores of people who are against them, especially Dalits, Adivasis and Minorities. In the past, BJP used ICE and NICE. ED and CBI were used to attack the opposition. It is not working anymore. Now, they are using the ECI itself, said Revanth Reddy. He alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar were creating two classes of citizens, one with voting rights and another without them, and warned that Dalits, Adivasis and minorities would be left without a voice. Gyanesh Kumar must resign. Modi and Shah must face justice for their crimes against India. Our leader Rahul ji is in Delhi to fight for our rights. We must all support him, he said. Revanth Reddy said he would convey the message of the people of Goa to Rahul Gandhi and called on the gathering to support the Congress leader. Expressing confidence about the Congress' prospects in the next Goa Assembly elections, he said, I also say this today - the fight against BJP will begin here in Goa. Next year, we will defeat BJP. Just like the Monsoon, which first comes to Kerala, then Goa, and only then reaches Delhi. Kerala is now with Congress, and I am confident Goa will be with us in 2027. After that, the Indian flag will be unfurled in Delhi. What begins in Goa will end at the Lal Qila when Rahul ji becomes Prime Minister of India, he said. Revanth Reddy once again congratulated the Goa Congress for organising the Goy Rakhonn Yatra and reiterated his confidence that the party would form the government in the state in 2027. I am confident Congress will come to power in 2027, he reiterated. (ANI)

articles.title: Houthis claim fresh wave of strikes on Saudi airports and oil facilities, call airspace
articles.summary: Yemeni Houthi forces claimed responsibility on Sunday for launching four major operations involving ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones against Saudi airports and energy infrastructure over a 24-hour period, declaring Saudi airspace unsafe with the explicit exception of the holy cities of Mecca and Medina. The rebel group's announcement came as King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh was struck again on Sunday, its second attack within 24 hours and third this week, when a projectile hit Terminal 4 and ignited a fire, following a devastating assault a day earlier that left 12 people dead and over 300 injured. According to an official statement shared by Houthi military spokesperson Brigadier General Yahya Saree on Telegram, the group framed the cross-border strikes as direct retaliation for recent coalition bombardment, stating, "In response to the brutal Saudi aggression against our country and our people, which launched 124 airstrikes in the past 24 hours, targeting the capital Sana'a and the governorates of Taiz, Ma'rib, Al-Jawf, Hajjah, Al-Hudaydah, and Sa'dah, bringing the total number of airstrikes since the beginning of the escalation against our country up to 2,058, committing massacres against our people, the majority of whose victims are women and children." Claiming extensive operations deep inside Saudi territory, the Houthi statement outlined the deployment of advanced weaponry across key targets. "With Allah's help, the Armed Forces carried out four qualitative operations in the past 24 hours using ballistic and cruise missiles and drones," the statement read. Detailing the individual operations, the rebel group claimed responsibility for targeting Saudi Arabia's main international hubs, asserting that air traffic was crippled in both the capital and the Eastern Province. Regarding the assault on the capital's aviation facilities, the statement claimed, "The first operation targeted in three phases King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh starting the evening before last, resulting in the disruption of air traffic and the complete closure of the airport." The statement further claimed a separate strike targeting Dammam's primary airport, noting, "The fourth operation targeted King Fahd International Airport in Dammam. The strike was direct and resulted in the disruption of air traffic at the airport." In addition to aviation targets, the rebel group claimed precise strikes against state oil giant Saudi Aramco's energy infrastructure in the Eastern Province. Describing the attack on gas infrastructure, the spokesperson stated, "The second operation targeted the Shugadam gas facility belonging to Aramco in the Eastern Province, and the strike was accurate, thanks be to Allah, and resulted in large fires breaking out at the targeted site." Regarding energy processing assets, the statement added, "The third operation targeted the Aramco Tanajib oil refinery in the Eastern Province. The strike was also accurate, thanks be to Allah, and resulted an ignition in it." The movement also claimed responsibility for military strikes against troop concentrations, stating, "In another development, our armed forces carried out a precise targeting operation against Saudi enemy buildups in the Ras al-Ara and al-Saqiya areas with six ballistic missiles and two drones, and the strikes were accurate, thanks be to Allah, and resulted in killing and wounding dozens of the enemy troops." Amid the military escalation, the Houthis issued a broad warning to international airlines, foreign workers, and commercial travellers to avoid Saudi aviation hubs, declaring Saudi airspace unsafe with the explicit exception of the holy cities of Mecca and Medina. "We reiterate our warning to all international companies, experts, employees, workers, and travellers from all over the world to not operate flights to Saudi airports, as they are unsafe, except for the airports and airspace of the holy cities of Mecca and Medina," the statement read. Vowing to maintain military pressure across the border until regional operations cease, the group concluded,"The Yemeni Armed Forces will continue their escalating operations deep inside Saudi, imposing the equation of "a blockade for a blockade" and "an escalation for an escalation" and targeting Saudi enemy reinforcements until the aggression ceases and the siege on our dear people is lifted." The statement comes as King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi capital was targeted in a fresh assault on Sunday, marking the second attack on the facility within 24 hours, as air defence forces intercepted a cruise missile and emergency responders tackled a fire sparked by an incoming projectile. The latest strike comes a day after a devastating attack at the same airport left 12 people dead and over 300 injured, severely disrupting international air traffic across the region. Confirming the fresh aerial threat, the Official Spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen, Major General Turki Al-Malki, stated that Saudi air defences successfully intercepted an incoming missile in the immediate vicinity of the capital's main aviation hub, according to statements reported by the Saudi Press Agency (SPA). "Official Spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen Major General Turki Al-Malki stated that the air defence intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile in the vicinity of King Khalid International Airport," the Saudi Press Agency reported. The interception followed an earlier breach at the complex where an incoming weapon struck passenger infrastructure, igniting a blaze inside the facility. Earlier, Major General Al-Malki stated that "Terminal 4 at King Khalid International Airport was struck by an unidentified projectile, resulting in a fire," adding that "the relevant authorities are currently responding to the incident." Emergency services and first responders were deployed to contain the blaze and secure the terminal. The back-to-back strikes highlight a sharp escalation in regional aerial attacks targeting critical civilian and aviation infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. This development unfolded as Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV reported that Saudi forces had initiated a fresh barrage of air and missile strikes across territories controlled by the group in Yemen, striking Sanaa International Airport in the capital, regions near the strategic Bab al-Mandeb Strait and various northern provinces. However, the Saudi-led coalition has not yet confirmed this strike. International condemnation has intensified following an attack carried out by Houthi forces targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, which sparked widespread global concern amid ongoing regional hostilities. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has strongly condemned the deadly "terrorist" attack, extending Israel's condolences to the victims' families while calling for regional unity against shared security threats. The statement, issued by the Israeli Prime Minister's Office, denounced the strike and emphasised the necessity of a decisive response to terror across the Middle East. "I condemn in the strongest possible terms the horrific terrorist attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, which claimed the lives of 12 innocent people and injured hundreds more," Netanyahu stated. Expressing solidarity with those affected by the fatal assault, the Israeli Prime Minister extended his sympathy to the families of the victims and those recovering from their injuries, stating, "On behalf of the people of Israel, I extend our deepest condolences to the families of those murdered and our wishes for a full recovery to the injured." Framing the assault as a broader attempt to destabilise the region, Netanyahu stressed that extremist threats require resolute action from regional actors. "Terrorism targets innocent people and seeks to spread fear and instability. It must be confronted with resolve," he said. Looking ahead at regional security dynamics, Netanyahu reaffirmed Israel's vision for a collaborative security architecture across the Middle East, saying,"Israel looks forward to a strong Middle East-one that stands united against threats, protects its people, and builds a future of security, cooperation, and prosperity for all the peoples of our region." On the other hand, US President Donald Trump stated that Washington was evaluating whether to join Saudi Arabia's strikes against Yemen's Houthi rebels following the lethal assault on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport. When asked if a decision had been made to participate in the Saudi strikes, Trump stated, "We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack. We will make a decision. We move very quickly." He further added, "Look, the Saudis are good fighters. But I think the attack was a terrible thing." US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the attack a "blatant disregard for innocent civilian life" and affirmed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and its people. "The United States strongly condemns the recent attacks on the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia by the terrorist Houthis, including today's strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that took numerous innocent lives, including an American citizen. These reprehensible attacks demonstrate a blatant disregard for innocent civilian life. They must stop now. We stand with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and its people and extend our condolences to the victims and their families," Rubio wrote in a post on X. In response to the escalation, the US Mission in Saudi Arabia issued a security alert on Sunday, directing American nationals to steer clear of King Khalid International Airport and adjacent zones following the October 10 strikes. The mission also cautioned travellers to exercise extreme vigilance at major Saudi airports, warning of potential flight cancellations, airspace restrictions and travel disruptions, while advising passengers to verify flight statuses directly with operators. Furthermore, the mission announced that US government personnel stationed in Saudi Arabia need special authorisation to use King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, alongside facilities in Jeddah and Dammam. These developments are anticipated to heighten pressure on Riyadh's international partners, including the United States, to extend military backing as the Kingdom intensifies operations against the Houthis. According to figures released by the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation, the 12 victims who died in the Saturday afternoon strike comprised four Saudi nationals alongside eight foreign residents, two from Bangladesh and one each from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan. Medical personnel are treating the 309 wounded individuals across multiple hospitals, with some patients listed in serious condition. Subsequently, the Indian authorities are coordinating with the Saudi authorities regarding the 11 nationals injured, out of which one succumbed to injuries, in the "dastardly attack" targeting King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi capital of Riyadh. In a post on X, the Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia said that it has been following up with the authorities after the attack, noting that the embassy officials also reached out to the hospital authorities where the injured Indian nationals are being treated. This came after India strongly condemned the deadly strike targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, while affirming its firm solidarity with Saudi Arabia in protecting its sovereignty. New Delhi asserted that the assault on civilian areas and vital installations was entirely unjustifiable. In the statement, the Ministry of External Affairs noted, "The repeated attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are completely unacceptable and must cease immediately." Reiterating India's diplomatic position, the MEA added, "We stand in solidarity with the people and the government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty, and hope that peace and normalcy return to the region at the earliest." Additionally, Dhaka issued a stern warning that it will take all necessary measures to protect Islamic holy sites in Mecca and Medina if they come under threat, following the deadly Houthi strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that killed two Bangladeshi pilgrims and forced the temporary suspension of all flights between Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia. "Bangladesh strongly and unequivocally condemns the deadly Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on 10 October 2026, which resulted in casualties, including the tragic loss of two Bangladeshi nationals, and left numerous others injured, many of them critically. Bangladesh mission in Riyadh is in contact with the Saudi authorities to obtain details of the deceased and injured Bangladeshis and to facilitate necessary assistance to those affected," the statement from the Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs read. Weighing in on the incident, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres took to social media to express his outrage over the offensive. In a post on X, he stated, "I am deeply shocked by and strongly condemn Saturday's lethal attack by the Houthis on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, which reportedly killed 12 people and injured hundreds of civilians. Attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are a violation of international law. These attacks must cease immediately." The strike follows a string of recent attacks directed at King Khalid International Airport over the past week. The Houthis previously claimed responsibility for assaults on the facility that left three Saudis dead, including a pilot. This surge in violence has also targeted other Saudi airfields, military installations and petroleum infrastructure, following a major military offensive initiated against the Houthis by a Saudi-led coalition the previous week. (ANI)

articles.title: Arunachal Pradesh Cabinet congratulates PM Modi on completing 25 Years as head of government
articles.summary: The Arunachal Pradesh Cabinet, led by Chief Minister Pema Khandu, on behalf of the people of the state, on Sunday joined crores of Indians in celebrating Prime Minister Narendra Modi completing 25 years of continuous service as head of government on October 7. PM Modi took the oath as Chief Minister of Gujarat on October 7, 2001 and continued through his service as Prime Minister of India from May 26, 2014 onwards. His third consecutive term began on June 9, 2024. In a press release issued by the CMO, Arunachal Pradesh stated that the state cabinet recorded that, across PM Modi's journey, his responsibilities have grown while his devotion to Bharat Mata has remained constant. From his early work at the grassroots to leadership of a state and the nation, the spirit of Seva Hi Samarpan has consistently guided his public life. Describing himself as the Pradhan Sevak, he placed service at the centre of governance and worked with discipline, perseverance and tireless dedication under the mantra of 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas and Sabka Prayas'. "The Cabinet highlighted the national transformation achieved under his leadership, from welfare, economic strength and national security to technology, infrastructure and renewed pride in India's heritage. Decisive actions, including the abrogation of Article 370, the replacement of colonial-era laws with the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Goods and Services Tax and next-generation GST 2.0 reforms, reflect a consistent commitment to national interest. The Cabinet also expressed its collective profound gratitude to the Prime Minister for launching the next-gen GST 2.0 reforms and the GST Bachat Utsav during his visit Itanagar on 22 September 2025, the first day of the pious occasion of Navratri. It is particularly significant that this resolution of the Cabinet was passed on 11th October, the first day of Navratri this year," said in the CMO Arunachal Pradesh statement. It also stated that Arunachal Pradesh has been a proud partner in this developmental journey. The State achieved 100 per cent saturation under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana, covering more than 8.57 lakh beneficiaries. Around 55,000 families received pucca houses registered in the names of women, while 2.28 lakh houses received functional household tap connections, making Arunachal Pradesh the first State in the North East to achieve 100% saturation under the Jal Jeevan Mission. More than 2.26 lakh families are covered under AB PM-JAY and CMAAY, providing cashless treatment of up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year. "The Prime Minister's focus on Annadata, Nari Shakti and Yuva Shakti has strengthened livelihoods and opened new opportunities across the State and throughout the nation. More than 1.14 lakh farmers from Arunachal Pradesh have been enrolled under PM-KISAN, with over Rs 150 crore transferred directly to their bank accounts. Nearly one lakh women have been mobilised into 15,999 Self-Help Groups; more than 16,000 have become Lakhpati Didis, with 36,000 more identified to reach this goal. 50 government schools have been upgraded into Golden Jubilee Model Schools, 58 Khelo India Centres now reach every district, and 156 startups have been supported with seed funding of more than Rs 5.59 crore, of which 45.5% are led by women," the CMO said. The Cabinet also noted the remarkable infrastructure transformation in Arunachal Pradesh. The Sela and Nechiphu tunnels have enhanced all-weather connectivity, strengthened strategic mobility and promoted tourism. Donyi Polo Airport, the State's first greenfield airport, can handle one million passengers a year, while Tezu Airport has been upgraded with a new terminal building. Under the Vibrant Villages Programme, 455 villages across 11 districts were selected in Phase I, with 1,022 km of roads worth Rs 2,205 crore approved to connect 126 border villages. A further 122 villages along the Myanmar and Bhutan borders have been included in Phase II, making frontier communities partners in development and national security," CMO Arunachal Pradesh stated in the press statement. It further stated that Arunachal Pradesh is also emerging as a future powerhouse of India. "The 2,000 MW Subansiri Lower Hydroelectric Project has been developed at a cost of Rs 30,071 crore, with 4 units commissioned and the remaining units expected shortly. Investment of more than Rs 52,000 crore has been approved for 5 additional hydropower projects that will generate almost 4,000 MW of renewable energy and support India's net zero goals. The Cabinet further expressed gratitude for the support in recognition, preservation and promotion of Arunachal Pradesh's rich indigenous, tribal and Buddhist heritage, cultures and traditions. 20 indigenous products have secured Geographical Indication tags. The Union Budget for 2026-27 announced a scheme to develop Buddhist circuits in six Northeastern States, including Arunachal Pradesh, while rare manuscripts and medical manuscripts are being documented and digitised under the Gyan Bharatam Mission," it said. "Under the Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment, Rs 4,900 crore has been allocated to Arunachal Pradesh under the Pride of Hills component. The Cabinet collectively renewed its commitment and resolve to build upon these achievements to form a strong foundation for the national resolve of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. It extended heartfelt congratulations to Narendra Modi, expressed profound gratitude for his life of service and tireless dedication, and reaffirmed Arunachal Pradesh's resolve to work under his guidance towards a prosperous, secure, self-reliant and developed India," said in the press statement. In other decisions, the Cabinet also approved a series of decisions aimed at strengthening higher and technical education, improving healthcare services, expanding support for women in distress, and streamlining administrative and institutional frameworks across the state. Among the key decisions, the Cabinet approved uniform, merit-based recruitment rules for several teaching and technical positions in government engineering and polytechnic colleges. In a significant step towards standardising recruitment in technical education institutions, the Cabinet approved recruitment rules for 12 categories of posts in government engineering and polytechnic colleges in accordance with the applicable All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) Regulations of 2019. The approved rules cover the posts of Principal in government polytechnic colleges and government engineering colleges; Assistant Professor, Associate Professor and Professor in government engineering colleges; Workshop Superintendent, Assistant Librarian, Laboratory Assistant, Senior Technical Assistant and System Analyst in government engineering colleges; and Head of Department (Civil Engineering) in government polytechnic colleges. The rules are intended to establish a transparent, merit-based and uniform mechanism for appointments, in line with the AICTE Diploma and Degree Regulations, 2019. To strengthen support for women facing distress and emergencies, the State Cabinet approved the creation of 20 posts to operationalise the Women Helpline-181 scheme, in accordance with Mission Shakti guidelines. Women Helpline-181 is a toll-free, round-the-clock service intended to provide emergency assistance and immediate response to women in distress, while connecting them with services such as medical care, shelter, legal aid, emotional support and guidance. The State Cabinet approved the renaming of Government College, Seppa, in East Kameng district, as Donglo Sonam Government College, Wessang, in honour of Late Donglo Sonam, recognised for his contribution to the growth and development of East Kameng district and Arunachal Pradesh. The State Cabinet also approved the naming of the Government Higher Secondary School, Daporijo, as the Lt Punji Mara Government Higher Secondary School, Daporijo and the naming of the Government Model Degree College, Daporijo, as the Popak Bage Government Model Degree College, Reempu Yorlo. The State Cabinet approved enhancement of grade pay for different categories of posts under the National Leprosy Elimination Programme (NLEP) in the Department of Health and Family Welfare. The decision seeks to address concerns regarding wage parity and fairness, improve staff morale and productivity, and strengthen the delivery of patient care and rehabilitation services. In another healthcare-related decision, the Arunachal Pradesh Cabinet approved the creation of five posts of Food Safety Officer, Group B, Gazetted Non-Ministerial. The new posts are intended to address manpower gaps in the State's food-law enforcement machinery and strengthen food-safety monitoring and enforcement to protect public health. (ANI)

articles.title: Revanth Reddy exudes confidence in Congress
articles.summary: Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy on Sunday expressed confidence that the Congress would come to power in Goa in the 2027 Assembly elections, saying he sensed the same optimism in the state that he had experienced in Telangana ahead of the 2023 polls. He urged voters to support the Congress's 'Hand' symbol and alleged that smaller parties emerging in Goa were being propped up by the BJP to divide votes. Addressing a gathering as part of the Congress' Goy Rakhonn Yatra, Revanth Reddy appealed to the people not to vote for smaller parties, claiming that their votes would ultimately benefit the BJP. They are here to divide the people. Any vote for them is a vote for BJP. This time, I urge the people of Goa, vote only for the Hand symbol, he said. Drawing a comparison between the Congress and the BJP through the Ramayan, the Telangana Chief Minister said, Ravan is BJP, which is dividing the people, and Ram is Congress. If you want to defeat Ravan, you have to support Ram, he said. Revanth Reddy said South Goa had traditionally been a Congress stronghold but alleged that the emergence of smaller parties could help the BJP retain power if voters did not support the Congress. Emphasising the need for voters to make their choice carefully, he said, Without voting for the Hand symbol, you cannot defeat BJP. Think twice before you vote. Who do you want running this state? Drug lords? Builder mafia? If you make a mistake once, you can move on. If you make it twice, you can still correct it. If you make the same mistake thrice, not even God can save us, he said. He said that while Congress leader Rahul Gandhi was working to unite people, the BJP was attempting to divide them. Revanth Reddy also explained why he was representing Rahul Gandhi at the gathering, saying the Congress leader had been required to remain in Delhi to lead the party's fight against the Union government. But yesterday, I got a call from Shri Mallikarjun Kharge ji. He said Rahul ji is needed in Delhi, where he is leading the fight for our country. Kharge ji told me to represent Rahul ji here. Rahul ji told him that Congress party workers in Goa are waiting. I am here as a messenger and representative of Rahul ji, he said. He described Rahul Gandhi as leading the youth, the Opposition and the country in a fight against what he called the corrupt dictatorship of the Modi government. Congratulating Goa Assembly Leader of Opposition Yuri Alemao and Goa Pradesh Congress Committee president Girish Chodankar for organising the yatra, Revanth Reddy conveyed greetings from Telangana and recalled the Congress' campaign ahead of the 2023 Assembly elections in his state. As Chief Minister of Telangana, I bring love and greetings from the people of Telangana. I remember how we, too, in Telangana had done a similar padayatra. I also note that there is optimism in the air here in Goa. It is the same optimism I found in Telangana ahead of the Assembly elections in 2023, when we won and formed the government there, he said. He said people were clear that the BJP government should not be allowed to return to power for a third term in Goa and alleged that the state's land was being transferred to others. I asked someone in a temple who their CM was. They told me the CM's name was 'Property Sawant'. The people of Goa elected him to lead the state, but that's not what he is doing. He is selling and giving away the land of Goa to others, said the Chief Minister. Revanth Reddy also raised concerns over unemployment and drug use among Goa's youth, recounting a conversation he had with a young person earlier in the day. He said things are very bad; there are no jobs. Then what are they doing, I asked. He said they are handling the stress badly and the youth are indulging in drugs. Goa has become a den of drugs, he said. Comparing the situation with Hyderabad before the Congress came to power in Telangana in 2023, he said his government had established the EAGLE force, an elite team of officers tasked with eradicating drugs in the state. After we took charge, I created the EAGLE force, an elite group of officers to eradicate drugs in Telangana. I came to know that a lot of the drugs are coming from Goa. We sent a team to Goa, and we found a large network of smugglers here, he said. He challenged Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant to explain why the state government had not taken effective action against drug trafficking, despite the Centre's stated objective of making India drug-free. The whole of the Indian government is on your side. The Prime Minister and Home Minister are saying Nasha Mukt Bharat. My question is simple - why are you not implementing it in Goa? It is because you are making money off drugs, he said. Questioning the BJP government's ability to tackle the problem, he asked whether Goa's association with drugs was good for the state and why the authorities had failed to control the issue despite the Enforcement Directorate (ED), the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and other agencies being under the BJP's control. BJP has ruined Goa, he declared. The Telangana Chief Minister also accused the BJP-led Union government of undermining democracy and alleged that the Election Commission of India (ECI) was being misused to remove voters from electoral rolls through the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government is destroying democracy in India. They have destroyed the Election Commission. They are misusing SIR to remove the votes of crores of people who are against them, especially Dalits, Adivasis and Minorities. In the past, BJP used ICE and NICE. ED and CBI were used to attack the opposition. It is not working anymore. Now, they are using the ECI itself, said Revanth Reddy. He alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar were creating two classes of citizens, one with voting rights and another without them, and warned that Dalits, Adivasis and minorities would be left without a voice. Gyanesh Kumar must resign. Modi and Shah must face justice for their crimes against India. Our leader Rahul ji is in Delhi to fight for our rights. We must all support him, he said. Revanth Reddy said he would convey the message of the people of Goa to Rahul Gandhi and called on the gathering to support the Congress leader. Expressing confidence about the Congress' prospects in the next Goa Assembly elections, he said, I also say this today - the fight against BJP will begin here in Goa. Next year, we will defeat BJP. Just like the Monsoon, which first comes to Kerala, then Goa, and only then reaches Delhi. Kerala is now with Congress, and I am confident Goa will be with us in 2027. After that, the Indian flag will be unfurled in Delhi. What begins in Goa will end at the Lal Qila when Rahul ji becomes Prime Minister of India, he said. Revanth Reddy once again congratulated the Goa Congress for organising the Goy Rakhonn Yatra and reiterated his confidence that the party would form the government in the state in 2027. I am confident Congress will come to power in 2027, he reiterated. (ANI)
